where.screen_path: library + feature internals (no UI this turn)

summary: Phase 5c-i-γ — wire the transport into the wallet without leaking keys. Wallet gained signDigest + nip44EncryptTo + nip44DecryptFrom; private keypair converted to a true JS #private field (D-03 now mechanically enforced at runtime, not just TS-private at compile time). buildEvent takes a sign-callback; sendEnvelopeTo/subscribeInbox take a Wallet. New connectWallet helper is the one-call entry point a UI layer will use. 6 new tapit-attest tests + 2 new wallet tests; all eight gates green; pushed branch-only.

why.text: The transport feature shipped last cut with a raw-keys API, which the doctrine D-03 (keys never leave the wallet unencrypted) forbids in a wired-up system. This cut routes all peer-encryption + Nostr-event-signing through the Wallet so the private key stays inside the Wallet instance. The keypair-to-#private upgrade was triggered by the grounding gate: a test I wrote asserted that wallet.keypair was undefined, and it failed — TS-private is compile-time only, the keypair was accessible from outside. Converted to JS-#private so the rule is enforced by the runtime, not just documented.

outcome.notes: Pushed to claude/compare-library-wallet-OW5FF as commit 25be3ba. NOT pushed to main — operator has not said the word for this cut. Branch is now three commits ahead of main: 5c-i-α (NIP-44 primitive), 5c-i-β (transport wire), 5c-i-γ (Wallet wire-up). No WalletProvider integration yet — that lands with 5c-i-δ alongside an operator opt-in toggle, since enabling the transport by default would expose the wallet's pubkey to public relays on every unlock. Pre-existing tapit-attest encryption tamper-byte flake (1/256) still relevant from previous sessions.

uncertainty: The transport-to-wallet seam is now correct and testable, but it has not been used by any real UI flow yet. The actual integration into WalletProvider (5c-i-δ) will need a settings opt-in, an inbox-state slot in the wallet context, and a routing component that surfaces incoming envelopes — none of which exists yet. NIP-44 interop against the upstream reference vectors still outstanding.
ripple: tapit-attest — new public surface (signDigest method, nip44EncryptTo, nip44DecryptFrom); private keypair is now JS-#private (no caller was reading it from outside, verified by grep before the change)
transport feature — public API changed (sendEnvelopeTo and subscribeInbox now take Wallet); no consumers outside the feature's own tests yet
next: Cut Phase 5c-i-δ — wire connectWallet into WalletProvider behind a settings opt-in toggle, expose inbox envelopes via WalletContext, and surface them in the UI (e.g. a People-tab notification or an absorb-modal route). Also: NIP-44 reference-vector cross-check before any encrypted messages hit a real relay.
